label: Pricing
seo_description: Compare Starter, Growth, and Enterprise capabilities. Indicative bands and quote-based packaging—final terms confirmed during procurement.
headline: Plans shaped around how schools actually operate.
subheadline: Starter for digitizing core operations, Growth for full admissions-to-reporting cycles, Enterprise for multi-campus governance. All commercial terms are confirmed in writing—never implied by this page alone.

segments.title: Starter
segments.body: Core records, attendance, communications, and straightforward reporting for schools beginning digitization.

segments.title: Growth
segments.body: Admissions pipelines, fees and invoicing, grading and report cards, analytics, and richer portal adoption.

segments.title: Enterprise
segments.body: Many campuses, one governance layer—group policy and reporting without HQ overriding local calendars, fees, or assessment rules. Offline sync, integrations, and audit depth per campus.

faqs.question: Are the currency amounts on this page final prices?
faqs.answer: No. The switcher shows indicative per-student bands for planning conversations only. Your quote reflects student count, modules, campuses, implementation, and regional tax rules.

faqs.question: Which plan fits a single-campus school?
faqs.answer: Starter focuses on digitizing records, attendance, communications, and baseline portals; Growth unlocks admissions depth and billing sophistication.

faqs.question: When should schools choose Enterprise?
faqs.answer: When you run many campuses under one governance layer—shared policy and visibility without overriding each campus’s local calendar, currency, or compliance posture.

faqs.question: Can we pilot before expanding?
faqs.answer: Yes—begin with a bounded rollout and expand modules once stakeholders validate workflows.
